answer.rationale: Write-path p99 started climbing ~30 minutes after the deploy and is now 5x target, so the release is the strongest causal candidate. memory_b1 is the matching playbook: rollback restored a stable prior build without dropping customer writes, which is the stated objective. Peak settlement load is a real confounder, so release attribution is not certain—verify b1’s archive before treating rollback as settled fact. Reject enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4 failing-fast would shed writes). Reject route_read_replicas (memory_b5 addressed report/dashboard read load, not this write-heavy settlement path). No regional signal for failover. One intervention only and the path is already badly degraded, so if rollback is confirmed the rollback itself should be a full revert, not a tiny cohort. Flag downstream value risk: release contents are unknown and undoing them mid-settlement could affect settlement outcomes if the deploy was load-bearing.
